elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Section 15.9 is retained unchanged: "will be governed by the internal laws of the State of Delaware, USA". No New York choice-of-law was proposed, so the preferred law element is unmet (Delaware is an accepted fallback law).

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: Revised 15.10.1 directs Disputes to "the state and federal courts located in the State of Delaware" with irrevocable submission to their exclusive jurisdiction; no New York County forum is designated.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 15.9: "governed by the internal laws of the State of Delaware, USA ... without regard to conflict of laws principles." Delaware sits squarely in the accepted fallback set; the ancillary reference to U.S. federal law for Patents/Trademarks is a subject-matter overlay, not a competing governing law.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: Revised 15.10.1: unresolved Disputes, "including any matter relating to breach or alleged breach of the ownership of intellectual property ... shall be brought exclusively in the state and federal courts located in the State of Delaware, and each Party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of such courts." The Delaware forum corresponds to the retained Delaware governing law. Mandatory ICDR arbitration is removed: 15.10.2.1/15.10.2.2 now operate "only if the Parties mutually agree in writing," so no residual mandatory arbitral merits forum remains. The retained carve-out for "preliminary injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction" is the customary temporary-relief exception and does not displace the exclusive merits forum. The narrow, pre-existing Section 7.5.5 AAA expert determination is confined to the single factual question of Material Impact on a Licensing Transaction and is not a general merits forum.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: Delaware law is untouched and the forum is now the exclusive Delaware state and federal courts, matching the chosen law. Preferred level is not reached because neither New York law nor a New York County forum was proposed \u2014 acceptable, since a clause at the fallback is a permissible landing zone.

Minimality holds. The edits are confined to forum words: (i) the referral sentence in 15.10.1 now names the Delaware courts instead of the ICDR; (ii) the old IP carve-out sentence's alternate forum ("a U.S. federal court of appropriate jurisdiction"), which would have created a broader competing merits forum and defeated exclusivity, is folded into the same Delaware exclusive-jurisdiction sentence rather than deleted in substance; (iii) 15.10.2.1/15.10.2.2 are conformed to consensual arbitration so the retained arbitration machinery does not contradict the new exclusive court forum. No survival tails, cost-shifting, jury-waiver, fee-shifting or other extras were added.

Favourable and unrelated mechanics survive: the Executive Officer escalation period, the Section 7.5.5 Material Impact referral, the preliminary-injunction right in any court of competent jurisdiction, the ICDR seat/rules text (now optional), and the Section 15.9 federal-law overlay for Patents and Trademarks are all preserved.

No dangling references result. The old cross-reference in 15.10.1 to "the arbitration clause set forth in Section 15.10.2" is removed in step with the change, and 15.10.2 remains internally coherent as an opt-in arbitration path triggered by later written agreement; the 15.10 preamble's "shall be resolved as follows" still has an operative path.

Residual point to watch (not a defect at this level): the retained 15.10.2.2 language "determination of the scope or applicability of this agreement to arbitrate" now applies only to Disputes the Parties have expressly agreed to arbitrate, so it does not reopen a mandatory arbitral gateway; if the counterparty argues otherwise, tighten by adding "solely with respect to Disputes submitted under Section 15.10.2.1".
